title: From ukulele and banjo to guitar; no teachers; hearing counterpoint in church
summary: He started on his sister's ukulele, moved to banjo and guitar, had no teacher available, and developed his own voicings, helped by hearing counterpoint at his mother's choir rehearsals.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Did you start on guitar or did you start on banjo?

No, I started on banjo -- I started on the ukulele. I'm getting ahead of my story. Actually, how I started playing a string instrument. My mother gave my sister, who also was a very fine pianist herself, marvelous pianist, she gave her a ukulele. And I took it and played it. My sister never could play it and I just took it and just played it. And this is how I think this is the beginning of the string instrument for me. From there I just -- I went to a banjo and I heard Eddie Lang and I made up my mind then that I was going to play guitar.

But the thing of it is nobody taught guitar then. You couldn't get a teacher. They -- everybody was groping, they didn't know too much about it themselves, so you just had to have some ingenuity and imagination, I should say, and do

these things yourselves. So this is why I had to teach myself. But even if I had had a teacher, I always heard certain sounds and I would have to voice the chords a certain way or else it would just bug me. So this is why my fingering was a little different, and --
You heard things that you hadn't heard (inaudible). you wanted...
anyone else play, and listening to your mother (inaudible) little children?
That's right, that's right. And so I had to do them myself, and I would sit and just figure out how to get the voicing. This is what I wanted to hear.
Did this start happening when you were (inaudible) little children?

Yes. And I guess I'm really getting ahead of my story, but you know my mother used to have a choir in Montgomery, and I would have to go to choir practice with her. And I used to sit in the balcony of this empty church while they were practicing, you know, rehearsing, on stage. And I used to hear all kind of sounds. They would sing certain kind of tunes, or songs, and I would sing just something contrapuntal to that, by myself. And I would hear different voices and I would go on a tangent from where they were going.
